title: Effects with useEffect: the dependency array, and cleaning up after yourself

videos.script:
A component's render must not change anything outside itself. But a real app has to talk to the outside: a server, the browser tab, the keyboard. Effects are where that happens, on purpose.

{{what}} An effect runs after React has put the render on the page. It can return a cleanup, which undoes what it started. And it has a list of what it depends on.

{{fetch}} You will fetch the planner's data from the server, with a screen for loading and a screen for failure. And you will see the request go out twice, which is strict mode testing your cleanup.

{{deps}} Then the dependency array. Leave one value out, and the tab's title stops following the week. Nothing fails. The linter is the only thing that notices.

{{cleanup}} Then a keyboard shortcut. Take its cleanup out, and one key press moves two weeks.

{{fails}} You will also break the address of the data, and find a failed request that answered with status two hundred.

{{notneeded}} And last, the effects you should not write at all.
